approach: Add `check_job_size(reading)` as one new `step!` in `refusing_check` (crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs), right after `check_prior_result_and_scope`. I measured the bound against HISTORY.txt first, and the earlier count-and-surface bound (8 files, 4 surfaces) failed that measurement: many single landed commits exceed it. Files per commit: 97d1e5c 13, f2d168c 21, 823dd32 about 27, 9a97e24 48. Under the old surface rule, dd4d76d had 6 surfaces and 69057b9 had 8. The only measure in that history that separates the two failed jobs from the landed ones is the number of separable surface groups. So the check has two parts. (1) Group rule: map each deliverable other than CHANGELOG.md to one of four groups: `config` (athena.toml or defaults.toml, from the existing `CONFIG_FILES`), `ci` (`.github/`), `docs` (`docs/` and root `*.md` files), `code` (everything else: crates, xtask, Cargo files, studies). Refuse when the reading spans more than 3 groups, that is all four: docs, config, CI and code. Both failed jobs span all four. I read every commit in HISTORY.txt (all 200): the most groups any landed commit spans is 3 (0406d25, 6f1b5f1, 7bc4b66, f339da5, 892cb1a: config, code and docs; c65e1f0 and 0cd0111: ci, docs and code). That is 0 of 200 landed commits refused by the group rule. Commit paths stand in for deliverables, so this is an estimate. (2) Count backstop: refuse above 30 non-changelog deliverables. This is the only count that does not refuse most landed commits: 1 of 200 (9a97e24, 48 paths) is refused, and 69057b9 (28), 823dd32 (27) and f2d168c (21) pass. A directory deliverable cannot hide size: the group rule does not depend on file counts, and a root directory deliverable (`.` or empty) counts as all four groups. Study readings and readings with a question are skipped, as in `check_scope_limit`. The declared share is 4% (an estimate, below the 25% reason threshold): 0 of 200 commits for the group rule plus the two known failed jobs, which may sit inside the 50-job replay window. Tests, corpus cases and one CHANGELOG entry follow the `check_scope_limit` precedent. No prompt, config or workflow file changes; the refusal text carries the repair. The existing `check_reading_size` (reading.rs:330) compares the reader's own forecast median wall time with the deadlines. It is a different measure: it trusts the reader's number and never looks at the deliverables. The new doc comment says so.

decisions.choice: Measure size as the number of separable surface groups (docs, config, ci, code) with a bound of 3, plus a high count backstop of 30 non-changelog deliverables. Both are named constants (`MAX_JOB_GROUPS`, `MAX_JOB_DELIVERABLES`). Both failed jobs are refused. Landed commits in HISTORY.txt are accepted, except 9a97e24 (48 paths), which the backstop refuses.
decisions.reason: I counted per commit in HISTORY.txt (lines 4-1566): the maximum number of groups on any landed commit is 3, while t67q and zaj2 each span docs, athena.toml, ci.yml and code (4 groups). Count alone separates nothing below 48. The groups are exactly the 'separable surfaces' that both introspections propose splitting on (config and CI versus code). Reusing `CONFIG_FILES` (checks.rs:577) keeps one definition of a config file.

rejected.option: Previous design: refuse above 8 deliverables or 4 surfaces (crate, docs, xtask, .github, root each a surface).
rejected.why: HISTORY.txt shows about 15 of the first 55 commits above 8 paths (97d1e5c 13, d6d2ad1 15, dd4d76d 12, e0f1a6f 10, 290f311 11, da17eda 12, f2d168c 21, 17e6d59 15, 823dd32 about 27, 9a97e24 48), and dd4d76d, d6d2ad1, 4bd944f, 69057b9, 6e7fd3a had 5 to 8 surfaces. It would refuse ordinary landed jobs, and the replay holds a candidate above the declared share plus 5 points.

rejected.option: Count the reader's criteria or request words.
rejected.why: A proxy. The deliverable list is the real measure, and the request text can be short for a large job.
It refuses 14 or more landed commits in the history and still misses a small job that crosses four groups, the t67q shape (9 paths).

rejected.option: Treat xtask or docs as groups of their own (up to 5 groups).
rejected.why: 6f1b5f1 (config, code, docs, xtask/shard-timings.txt) and 3 or 4 other landed commits would reach 4 groups. xtask is Rust code, so it is part of `code`.

decisions.choice: The share is declared as 'expected 4% of newly refused readings, an estimate and not a measurement'. The doc comment, CHANGELOG item and criterion carry it, with the HISTORY.txt measurement (0 of 200 landed commits by groups, 1 of 200 by count) and the note that commit paths stand in for deliverables.
decisions.reason: The replay (replay.rs:161, 305) holds a candidate whose new refusals exceed the declared share plus 5 points, or 10% with none declared. 4% plus 5 gives 9%. A share of 25% or less needs no reason text (replay.rs:165, 204). The two known failed jobs are at most 2 of the 50 readings in the window, so 4% is the upper figure of the evidence.

rejected.why: It was not tied to any measurement.
Both failed jobs are expected to be refused if they sit in the replay window, so 0% understates it.

decisions.choice: A directory deliverable is assigned a group by its first path component (`crates/athena-core/src/` is code). A root directory deliverable (`.`, `./`, empty) counts as all four groups.
decisions.reason: This answers the critic's finding that a directory deliverable hides size. The group rule does not depend on how many files a path stands for, so `crates/athena-core/src/` listed with docs, athena.toml and a workflow is still four groups. The only way to claim every group in one path is the root, which is made to count as all of them.

rejected.option: Count a directory as the bound's worth of files.
rejected.why: It would refuse any reading that lists a directory, for example `crates/athena-cli/tests/`, which three landed commits touch. The count rule is only a backstop, and the group rule is where size is judged.

decisions.choice: Skip readings whose capability is not `change` or that carry a question, as `check_scope_limit` does (checks.rs:706). Place `step!(check_job_size(reading));` second, after `check_prior_result_and_scope`.
decisions.reason: A study reading has no change to measure, and a reading with a question has no accepted scope. A reading that must be split makes the later repairs moot, so the reader should be told to split first. The retry check stays first because it needs the earlier attempt. I read the adjacency tests: they pin survey to history_fixture, outcome_state to environment_reach, governance to outcome_state and environment_reach to defined_terms, not this position.

rejected.why: The reader would first repair scope-limit text in a reading that is then refused for size, costing a read round.

decisions.choice: The producer no-change guard stays out of scope; the refusal error text states the repair.
decisions.reason: The brief puts `run/producer.rs` and `run/send_back.rs` out of scope, and the gate acts before dispatch, so no producer run is spent.

rejected.why: It acts after the run is spent and is out of scope.

risks.risk: The group rule is calibrated on two failed jobs and 200 landed commits. A large job that spans only three groups (for example config, ci and code with 25 files) is not refused. The count backstop does not reach it either.
risks.mitigation: The check's doc comment and the CHANGELOG item list this as a known miss. The two bounds are named constants, so a later change is one line and the at-the-bound tests move with it. The producer no-change guard remains a separate follow-up outside this job.

risks.risk: The commit paths in HISTORY.txt stand in for reading deliverables, so the 0-of-200 figure is an estimate. The producer may have changed more files than the reading listed.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG item, doc comment and criterion label the figures an estimate and not a measurement. The verification replay over the last 50 accepted readings measures the real share and holds the candidate above the declared 4% plus 5 points.

risks.risk: An existing test reading is refused: it spans four groups or has more than 30 deliverables.
risks.mitigation: I searched readings with long deliverable lists in reading.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, steward.rs, run/tests.rs and drain.rs and found none above 3 paths. Criterion 6 runs the whole suite, and a failure names the reading. The fix is to shrink the fixture, never to raise the bound.

risks.risk: A reader retried after the refusal still lists all four groups and is refused again.
risks.mitigation: The error tells the reader to keep one dependency-ordered group and name the others in `out_of_scope`, which existing checks accept. `read_for` re-reads once with the refusal text. Automatic splitting stays out of scope.

risks.risk: Path forms are misclassified: `./` prefixes, directory deliverables, root files such as README.md or Cargo.lock, `studies/` and `xtask/shard-timings.txt`.
risks.mitigation: `job_group` normalizes with `normalized_path` first (checks.rs:775). It maps `athena.toml` and `defaults.toml` to config, a path under `.github/` to ci, `docs/` and any other root `.md` file to docs, and all else to code. `.`, `./` and empty map to all four groups. `job_size_bound_is_general` has a case for each form.

demonstrations.method: A unit test pins the doc comment and the CHANGELOG item. A corpus test pins that the declaration parses to the stated share. The second command is part of the first test group in the corpus binary, so it needs its own invocation.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core job_size_ && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus job_size_refusal_is_declared_intended
demonstrations.observes: The doc comment and the CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] item containing `reading::check_job_size` both contain the root-cause sentence, 'higher refusal rate is intended', 'expected 4% of newly refused readings', 'estimate', 'HISTORY.txt', 'more than 3 groups' and '30 deliverables'. The corpus test asserts `replay_declaration(&[criterion with that sentence], &[]).share == Some(4)`, as `design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended` does (refusal_corpus.rs:2771).
demonstrations.fails_without: A changelog item without the cause, the bound or the share fails the needle assertions. A doc without the sentence 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' fails the pin.
demonstrations.seam: `include_str!("reading/checks.rs")` and `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` as in reading.rs:8371 and 8382 (exist). `athena_core::reading::replay_declaration` is public and used at refusal_corpus.rs:2773 (exists). Tests are added in steps 5 and 7. No double.

demonstrations.method: The three gate commands Athena runs on the result.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. This covers every existing test that reaches the gate (reading.rs gate tests, run/tests.rs, steward.rs, athena-cli drain.rs, the briefs test that lists reading checks).
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting slip, a clippy lint (an unused constant or helper) or a regression in an existing test, for example an existing reading now refused as too large.
demonstrations.seam: The cargo commands themselves; nothing is injected.

open_questions: User: Criterion 3 asks that many deliverables in one crate are refused on count alone. HISTORY.txt shows landed single commits with 13, 21, about 27 and 48 non-changelog paths, so the count backstop is set at 30 and refuses 1 of 200 landed commits (9a97e24, 48 paths). Do you accept 30, or do you want a lower count and the measured false refusals that come with it?
